occupation: Laborer (1880); carpenter (1926); superintendent for the Ambrose West construction company; later employee of the Luzerne County Court House
summary: John's 2nd-great-grandfather; carpenter and construction superintendent of Plymouth and Wilkes-Barre who married into the Irish-Catholic Heffernans in 1892.
bio: Addison F. Pringle was born in Plymouth; his 1943 obituary gives 2 Dec 1868, FamilySearch gives Dec 1867, the Ancestry tree screenshots show 1867 (the transcription summary says 1868), and the 1880 census age of 15 implies about 1865, so his birth year should be treated as 1865-68 with 2 Dec 1868 preferred (obituary). In June 1880 he was a 15-year-old 'laborer' in the Plymouth Twp household of his father Andrew Pringle, laborer, while his 13-year-old brother Orange was a slate picker in a coal breaker. His mother later divorced his father and resumed the name Scott; Bradsby's 1893 sketch of her lists five living children and omits Addison, then about 25 and recently married (the reason is unknown - perhaps because he lived apart from her). On 29 Jun 1892 he married Catherine E. Heffernan at Plymouth. They had eight children (Genevieve, Joseph Vincent, Mary E., Anna Theresa, Florence, Helen, Francis, Catherine). He lived in Plymouth Twp in 1900, Larksville in 1910, Wilkes-Barre Ward 15 in 1920 and at 28 Huston St, Wilkes-Barre from 1926 to 1940. The 1926 licence calls him a carpenter (born Penna). His obituary says he was a superintendent for the Ambrose West construction company and later worked at the Luzerne County Court House (as had his father-in-law Andrew H. Heffernan). He died at Wilkes-Barre on 2 Sep 1943 (PA death index 1943: 'ADDISON F PRINGLE, WLKS BRE, P652, co. 40, 9-2-43, file 82141'). The obituary names his parents as 'Andrew Pringle and Catherine Scott Pringle, early residents of the West Side' and lists 'Mrs. William Meier, Wilkes-Barre' among survivors.
funFacts: At 15 in 1880 he was already a laborer; his brother Orange, 13, picked slate in a coal breaker.

Three generations held county jobs: father-in-law Andrew H. Heffernan ('attache of the Court house'), brother-in-law Thomas F. Heffernan (assistant county treasurer), and Addison himself at the Court House.
His son Francis's 1936 marriage licence (No. 1732, Luzerne) names his parents as 'Addison F.' and 'Catherine Heffernan'.
